newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, recovering from surgery, swaps hospitals.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, recovering from surgery, swaps hospitals.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, making a speedy recovery from open heart surgery, was moved on Friday from a specialist clinic to the more comfortable surroundings of Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital.
Eyewitnesses saw the presidential motorcade leave the Cardiology Research Centre, where Yeltsin had his quintuple bypass on Tuesday, soon after 11 a.m. (0800 GMT), heading for the nearby hospital.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said Yeltsin, 65, had been transferred and added that he expected the Russian president to make a speedy recovery.
"Now the president will be gaining strength very quickly," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Chernomyrdin as saying. The main task of those surrounding the president was to "save him from overload".
The prime minister took over for 23 hours while Yeltsin had his operation.
Doctors said on Thursday that Yeltsin was recovering well and was already walking around his hospital ward.

He could be carrying out most of his presidential duties within two weeks, although the doctors said Yeltsin would have to avoid straining himself too quickly and may need up to two months for a full convalescence.
Yeltsin had spent some time preparing for the multiple bypass operation in a suite at the Central Clinical Hospital in suburban Moscow. He was also treated there after two heart attacks last year.

Renat Akchurin, the Russian surgeon who led the operating team, told NTV television on Thursday that Yeltsin was recovering ahead of schedule and could be ready to talk in public as early as Friday or Saturday, indicating that a televised address might be on the cards.
Yeltsin has already chatted privately with Chernomyrdin as well as with family and friends.
